audit.corrected: Side moved to Kassadin, rating to 7/10, why rewritten to the Kassadin verdict.

audit.why: Spikes correct: Qiyana owns 1-6 and first item vs dashless pre-6 Kassadin; late flips at 2+ items / stacked R. All 4 spikes present.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldowns field had no numbers; Nether Blade auto-reset tell absent from the page.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s — the only reason the lane flips. Kassadin's burst opens with the Nether Blade (W) auto reset — the wind-up is the cue to step back. His Q grants a magic shield, but Qiyana is full AD so the shield does not blunt her combo.
audit.corrected: Numbers and the W-reset tell written into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.why: Pre-6 no dash, E Force Pulse 21s at rank 1 — the all-in windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The _missing rule claims Null Sphere is an interruptible channel.
audit.why: Riot's own text says Null Sphere INTERRUPTS channels; the 'channel' flag on it looks like a tooltip-parse misfire. Did not assert the interaction.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to items: each Riftwalk stack drops its cooldown toward 2 seconds until your combo can no longer land.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Check it before every step-up. - W Terrashape (element swap) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Kassadin Riftwalk: 5s at rank 1, 2s at rank 3 — pre-6 he has no dash at all; that is your whole window. - His Nether Blade auto-reset opens every trade: step back on the wind-up. - Your W is 7s, your R 120s — the ult answers fights, not waves.

edits.before: Grass-Q from stealth, E-ice the answer, auto, walk back into the hedge — terrain trades he experiences as ambush weather.
edits.after: Break his vision in grass mid-trade: your passive re-arms and his point-blank Nether Blade auto has to find you again first.

edits.before: E-ing in with no element loaded and his CC banked — Qiyana without terrain prep is a dagger doing improv.
edits.after: Force Pulse slows in a 400-range cone and his W auto chunks — open-ground duels give his combo full uptime.

edits.before: Late Qiyana flanks through her own R: shockwave the objective wall, string the stunned, and vanish into grass.
edits.after: Stacked Riftwalks at 2s cooldown blink through your combo — close the game before his two-item timing lands.
